one_liner: Header-only SIMD string kernels (search, hashing, sort, UTF-8) beating std::string::find and find_first_of.
what_it_does: Header-only C99 kernel library with a C++11 wrapper (sz::string_view / sz::string) that reimplements substring/byte-set search, hashing, lexicographic compare, sorting, set intersection, memory ops, and edit distances. The C++ types mirror std::string_view/std::string member surfaces, so existing code keeps working, but replacing std::string::find calls with sz::find/sz_find is a manual search-and-replace, not an ABI override.
how_it_is_fast: Per-ISA SIMD kernels (SSE4.2/AVX2/AVX-512 on x86, NEON/SVE/SVE2 on ARM, plus WASM SIMD128, RISC-V RVV, PowerPC VSX, LoongArch) selected at compile time or via a runtime dispatch table in the optional shared build. Needle-length-adaptive algorithm choice: brute-force SIMD comparisons at multiple needle offsets for short needles, Boyer-Moore-Horspool with a bad-character shift table and Raita-style character-anomaly detection for mid/long needles, and SWAR (64-bit word) fallback with no SIMD.
when_to_use: Hot substring search over large text buffers where std::string::find shows up in a profile
Splitting/tokenizing on multiple delimiter bytes (replacing find_first_of/strcspn) via sz_find_byteset
Multi-language pipelines that need identical search/hash/sort kernels across C/C++/Python/Rust/Go/Swift/JS/C#/Java
Unicode case-folding, segmentation, or normalization at C speed instead of ICU/ICU4X
Apple Silicon or ARM server targets, where the README reports the widest gap over the system libc strstr
when_not_to_use: Multi-pattern literal matching: no Aho-Corasick automaton is shipped; README points to hyperscan or pyahocorasick instead
Need a std::hash-compatible hasher: sz's hash is a separate AES-based non-standard function, not a std::hash specialization
Building for i386 — currently broken (open issue #341)
Need find_all() match offsets relative to the parent string — reported broken in open issue #278
Very short, early-diverging comparisons (equality/order checks) — README itself says vectorization is 'almost useless' there
Risk-averse adoption of sz::argsort right now — open crash report (#337) and an open UBSAN misaligned-write report (#279)

integration.dependencies: none (freestanding build available via SZ_AVOID_LIBC=1); optional precompiled shared library for runtime dispatch
integration.min_toolchain: C99 / C++11 minimum to compile; CI-validated on GCC 12+, Clang 16+, MSVC 2022, NVCC CUDA 12+ (GCC 10 and older fail STL insert conformance needed by the test suite)
integration.platforms: x86-64 (SSE4.2/AVX2/AVX-512 tiers), aarch64 (NEON/SVE/SVE2), WebAssembly (SIMD128 via wasm32-wasip1), RISC-V (RVV), PowerPC (VSX), LoongArch; i386 currently fails to build (issue #341)
integration.thread_safety: not documented explicitly as a guarantee; the library keeps no global/thread-local state and every allocating function takes an explicit sz_memory_allocator_t, which implies reentrant kernels
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: sz::string_view/sz::string implement the std::string_view/std::string member surface (data/size/substr/compare/iterators/operator<=>), so passing them around is drop-in, but calling the faster search itself means rewriting std::string::find(...) as sz::find(...)/sz_find(...)

gotchas: sz_find_byte_serial historically mis-compared bytes > 0x7F when compiled with -fsigned-char (issue #306, closed/fixed) — a signed-char caution sign for anyone pinning old versions
find_all() results reportedly cannot recover the match's position within the parent string (open issue #278)
sz::argsort has an open crash report (#337)
UBSAN reports a misaligned-address write in a SWAR code path (open issue #279)
pick_this_over_siblings_when: sse4-strstr is the closest sibling but covers only substring search as a single header with no bindings; pick StringZilla when you also need byte-set scanning, hashing, sorting, or non-C++ language bindings and can accept a larger, fast-moving dependency. Pick sse4-strstr instead when you want a small, frozen, single-purpose kernel to vendor with nothing else attached.
verified_claims_summary: README Performance table: finding the first occurrence of a ~5-byte random word, std::string::find (STL, GCC+glibc) hit 9.1 GB/s vs sz_find 21.0 GB/s (~2.3x) on an Intel Sapphire Rapids Xeon4, and 10.9 vs 37.1 GB/s (~3.4x) on Apple M5 Pro (Apple Clang+libc++). Splitting lines on \n/\r, std::string::find_first_of hit 1.1 GB/s vs sz_find_byteset 13.8 GB/s on Xeon4, and 4.1 vs 23.7 GB/s on M5 Pro.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-08-12, 3,563 stars, Apache-2.0); header-only core is easy to vendor ('copyable'), but several open bugs (i386 build failure, argsort crash, misaligned-write UBSAN report) mean trusting specific kernels rather than the whole surface unverified.
